content.user_title: Build Safer Systems with Memory Safety Patterns
content.value_statement: Memory errors and unsafe resource ownership can cause crashes, leaks, and data races. This skill applies proven patterns across C, C++, and Rust.
actual_capabilities: Explains RAII patterns for files, mutexes, and transactional rollback in C++.
Compares unique, shared, and weak pointer ownership models.
Demonstrates Rust ownership, borrowing, lifetimes, and synchronized sharing.
Shows structured cleanup patterns for manually managed C resources.
Reviews bounds checking and data race prevention approaches.
limitations: Does not execute sanitizers, compilers, or test suites.
Does not prove that a complete program is memory safe.
Examples require adaptation for project APIs and platform constraints.
C, C++, and Rust receive more coverage than managed languages.

use_cases.title: Review Systems Code
use_cases.description: Identify ownership, lifetime, cleanup, bounds, and synchronization risks in a focused code review.

use_cases.title: Design Resource Lifecycles
use_cases.description: Choose RAII, smart pointers, or explicit cleanup for files, sockets, memory, and locks.

use_cases.title: Learn Rust Ownership
use_cases.description: Understand moves, borrowing, lifetimes, reference counting, and thread-safe shared state through practical examples.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Memory Safety Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how [pattern] prevents [memory bug]. Include one concise example in [language] and list its main tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Review Resource Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this [C or C++] resource lifecycle. Find leak, double-free, and exception-safety risks, then recommend specific cleanup changes.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Ownership Designs
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare RAII, reference counting, and Rust ownership for this component: [description]. Recommend one model based on concurrency and lifetime needs.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Concurrent Memory Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this concurrent systems code for data races, invalid lifetimes, lock misuse, and unsafe sharing. Prioritize findings and propose verification steps.

output_examples.input: Review a C function that allocates a buffer, opens a file, and returns early after errors.
output: High priority: centralize cleanup so every failure path releases the buffer and file.
Initialize resource handles before acquisition and release each resource only when valid.
Verify the change with allocation-failure tests and AddressSanitizer.

output_examples.input: Choose an ownership model for a C++ object shared by worker tasks.
output: Use unique ownership when one component controls the lifetime and workers borrow within a guaranteed scope.
Use shared ownership only when tasks must extend the lifetime independently.
Use weak references for observers to prevent ownership cycles.

best_practices: State the resource owner and expected lifetime before selecting a pattern.
Provide the relevant code, language version, concurrency model, and failure behavior.
Verify recommendations with compiler warnings, sanitizers, and targeted tests.
anti_patterns: Do not assume smart pointers automatically make object graphs cycle free.
Do not use unchecked access or unsafe blocks without a documented invariant.
Do not apply examples unchanged without checking project APIs and error handling.

faq.question: Which languages does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on C, C++, and Rust, with general guidance that also applies to other systems languages.

faq.question: Can this skill prove my program is memory safe?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and review guidance, but verification still requires testing, analysis tools, and project-specific review.

faq.question: Does the skill run AddressSanitizer or Valgrind?
faq.answer: No. It can recommend commands and interpret supplied results, but it does not run tools by itself.

faq.question: Can it help migrate raw pointers to smart pointers?
faq.answer: Yes. It can map ownership roles and recommend unique, shared, or weak pointers based on actual lifetime requirements.

faq.question: Does it cover concurrent memory safety?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains atomics, mutexes, read-write locks, thread-safe sharing, and Rust data race prevention.

faq.question: What context improves the review?
faq.answer: Provide the code, language version, ownership expectations, thread model, error paths, and available test or sanitizer results.
